input.question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?
input.ground_truth: Nothing. In 2015 alone, airplanes [carried ~3.441B people](_URL_0_). Most of them have devices with radios (phones, tablets, laptops). Many of them simply forgot to turn it off. There has never been a single malfunction of any sort attributed to a GSM/UMTS/LTE or WiFi radio not turned off. As a side note, FAA does not prohibit cellphone (much less WiFi) operation during flight, see 14 CFR 91.21 (b)(5); FCC and carriers do.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your phone is like a little talker. When you are on an airplane, you need to tell your phone to be quiet so it doesn’t talk to the airplane’s “talkie” stuff and mess things up.

If you don’t tell your phone to be quiet (that’s what airplane mode is), your phone might try to talk to cell towers on the ground. That could be like lots of people talking at once and making a big mess, which could make the airplane’s talkie stuff confused.

But the *worst* thing that could happen is maybe the airplane’s talkie stuff doesn’t work right for a little bit, and the pilots have to fix it. But it’s very, very rare, and everyone is careful about this, so it’s not super scary. But it’s better to be safe and use airplane mode! ✈️📱🔇
